Tendency

TEN-dun-see (stress on TEN) · noun

Hear It

What It Means

a leaning toward acting or happening in a certain way, over and over

Billy has a tendency to wait until the last minute, yet he somehow still earns good grades.

Worked Example

Our dog has a tendency to hide shoes before thunderstorms, so we check the closet whenever clouds roll in.

One hidden shoe would just be an accident. The word tells you this leaning repeats often enough that the family plans around it - that repeated pull is the tendency.

How Tendency Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

leaning

leaning: a gentle pull toward one choice or direction

pattern

pattern: something that repeats in a way you can spot

Antonyms

dislike

dislike: a feeling of not enjoying or not wanting something

resistance

resistance: a pushing back against doing something

How Strong Is It? — impulse → tendency → habit

impulse vs. tendency

impulse vs. tendency: An impulse is weaker than a tendency: an impulse is a single sudden push to act that may never return, while a tendency is a leaning that shows up again and again.

habit vs. tendency

habit vs. tendency: A habit is stronger than a tendency: a tendency means you often lean a certain way, but a habit means the action has become automatic and happens almost without thought.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — tend

root — tend: to lean or stretch

suffix — ency

suffix — ency: the state or quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Join tend ('to lean or stretch') with -ency ('the state of') and you get 'the state of leaning': a tendency is the way a person or thing keeps leaning toward one behavior.

Use the root in a new word: intend

Use the root in a new word: intend: I intend to finish my project on Friday, and I am already leaning all my plans toward that goal.

Root Check

Word Choice

Tendency usually takes 'to' plus an action: a tendency to interrupt, a tendency to rust. It stays neutral or slightly negative, so writers pick it for leanings they are pointing out rather than praising. For a fully automatic behavior, habit is the stronger claim.
